1: use ruff_diagnostics::{AlwaysFixableViolation, Diagnostic, Edit, Fix};
2: use ruff_macros::{derive_message_formats, ViolationMetadata};
3: use ruff_python_ast::parenthesize::parenthesized_range;
4: use ruff_python_ast::{self as ast, Expr, Stmt};
5: use ruff_text_size::Ranged;
6: 
7: use crate::checkers::ast::Checker;
8: 
9: /// ## What it does
10: /// Checks for `for` loops that can be replaced with `yield from` expressions.
11: ///
12: /// ## Why is this bad?
13: /// If a `for` loop only contains a `yield` statement, it can be replaced with a
14: /// `yield from` expression, which is more concise and idiomatic.
15: ///
16: /// ## Example
17: /// ```python
18: /// for x in foo:
19: ///     yield x
20: /// ```
21: ///
22: /// Use instead:
23: /// ```python
24: /// yield from foo
25: /// ```
26: ///
27: /// ## Fix safety
28: /// This rule's fix is marked as unsafe, as converting a `for` loop to a `yield
29: /// from` expression can change the behavior of the program in rare cases.
30: /// For example, if a generator is being sent values via `send`, then rewriting
31: /// to a `yield from` could lead to an attribute error if the underlying
32: /// generator does not implement the `send` method.
33: ///
34: /// In most cases, however, the fix is safe, and such a modification should have
35: /// no effect on the behavior of the program.
36: ///
37: /// ## References
38: /// - [Python documentation: The `yield` statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-yield-statement)
39: /// - [PEP 380 – Syntax for Delegating to a Subgenerator](https://peps.python.org/pep-0380/)
40: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
41: pub(crate) struct YieldInForLoop;
42: 
43: impl AlwaysFixableViolation for YieldInForLoop {
44:     #[derive_message_formats]
45:     fn message(&self) -> String {
46:         "Replace `yield` over `for` loop with `yield from`".to_string()
47:     }
48: 
49:     fn fix_title(&self) -> String {
50:         "Replace with `yield from`".to_string()
51:     }
52: }
53: 
54: /// Rewrite a `for` loop that solely yields its target into a `yield from`.
55: pub(crate) struct YieldFromRewrite<'a> {
56:     stmt_for: &'a ast::StmtFor,
57: }
58: 
59: impl<'a> YieldFromRewrite<'a> {
60:     pub(crate) fn new(stmt_for: &'a ast::StmtFor) -> Self {
61:         Self { stmt_for }
62:     }
63: 
64:     /// UP028
65:     pub(crate) fn yield_in_for_loop(&self, checker: &mut Checker) {
66:         // Intentionally omit async contexts.
67:         if in_async_context(checker) {
68:             return;
69:         }
70: 
71:         let stmt_for = self.stmt_for;
72: 
73:         // If there is an else statement, don't rewrite.
74:         if !stmt_for.orelse.is_empty() {
75:             return;
76:         }
77: 
78:         // If there's any logic besides a yield, don't rewrite.
79:         let [body] = stmt_for.body.as_slice() else {
80:             return;
81:         };
82: 
83:         let Some(value) = yielded_value(body) else {
84:             return;
85:         };
86: 
87:         // If the target is not the same as the value, don't rewrite. For example, we should rewrite
88:         // `for x in y: yield x` to `yield from y`, but not `for x in y: yield x + 1`.
89:         if !is_same_expr(&stmt_for.target, value) {
90:             return;
91:         }
92: 
93:         // If any of the bound names are used outside of the yield itself, don't rewrite.
94:         if collect_names(value).any(|name| name_escapes_yield(checker, name)) {
95:             return;
96:         }
97: 
98:         let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(YieldInForLoop, stmt_for.range());
99:         let locator = checker.locator();
100:         let indexer = checker.indexer();
101:         let iter = stmt_for.iter.as_ref();
102:         let contents = locator.slice(
103:             parenthesized_range(
104:                 iter.into(),
105:                 stmt_for.into(),
106:                 indexer.comment_ranges(),
107:                 locator.contents(),
108:             )
109:             .unwrap_or(iter.range()),
110:         );
111:         let contents = format!("yield from {contents}");
112:         diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::unsafe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
113:             contents,
114:             diagnostic.range,
115:         )));
116:         checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
117:     }
118: }
119: 
120: fn in_async_context(checker: &Checker) -> bool {
121:     checker.semantic().in_async_context()
122: }
123: 
124: fn yielded_value(body: &Stmt) -> Option<&Expr> {
125:     let Stmt::Expr(ast::StmtExpr { value, range: _ }) = body else {
126:         return None;
127:     };
128:     let Expr::Yield(ast::ExprYield {
129:         value: Some(value),
130:         range: _,
131:     }) = value.as_ref()
132:     else {
133:         return None;
134:     };
135:     Some(value)
136: }
137: 
138: fn name_escapes_yield(checker: &Checker, name: &ast::ExprName) -> bool {
139:     checker
140:         .semantic()
141:         .current_scope()
142:         .get_all(name.id.as_str())
143:         // Skip unbound bindings like `del x`
144:         .find(|&id| !checker.semantic().binding(id).is_unbound())
145:         .is_some_and(|binding_id| {
146:             let binding = checker.semantic().binding(binding_id);
147:             binding.references.iter().any(|reference_id| {
148:                 checker.semantic().reference(*reference_id).range() != name.range()
149:             })
150:         })
151: }
152: 
153: /// Return `true` if the two expressions are equivalent, and both consistent solely
154: /// of tuples and names.
155: fn is_same_expr(left: &Expr, right: &Expr) -> bool {
156:     match (&left, &right) {
157:         (Expr::Name(left), Expr::Name(right)) => left.id == right.id,
158:         (Expr::Tuple(left), Expr::Tuple(right)) => {
159:             left.len() == right.len()
160:                 && left
161:                     .iter()
162:                     .zip(right)
163:                     .all(|(left, right)| is_same_expr(left, right))
164:         }
165:         _ => false,
166:     }
167: }
168: 
169: /// Collect all named variables in an expression consisting solely of tuples and
170: /// names.
171: fn collect_names<'a>(expr: &'a Expr) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = &'a ast::ExprName> + 'a> {
172:     Box::new(
173:         expr.as_name_expr().into_iter().chain(
174:             expr.as_tuple_expr()
175:                 .into_iter()
176:                 .flat_map(|tuple| tuple.iter().flat_map(collect_names)),
177:         ),
178:     )
179: }

1: use ruff_python_trivia::{BackwardsTokenizer, CommentRanges, SimpleTokenKind, SimpleTokenizer};
2: use ruff_text_size::{Ranged, TextLen, TextRange};
3: 
4: use crate::AnyNodeRef;
5: use crate::ExpressionRef;
6: 
7: /// Returns an iterator over the ranges of the optional parentheses surrounding an expression.
8: ///
9: /// E.g. for `((f()))` with `f()` as expression, the iterator returns the ranges (1, 6) and (0, 7).
10: ///
11: /// Note that without a parent the range can be inaccurate, e.g. `f(a)` we falsely return a set of
12: /// parentheses around `a` even if the parentheses actually belong to `f`. That is why you should
13: /// generally prefer [`parenthesized_range`].
14: pub fn parentheses_iterator<'a>(
15:     expr: ExpressionRef<'a>,
16:     parent: Option<AnyNodeRef>,
17:     comment_ranges: &'a CommentRanges,
18:     source: &'a str,
19: ) -> impl Iterator<Item = TextRange> + 'a {
20:     let right_tokenizer = if let Some(parent) = parent {
21:         // If the parent is a node that brings its own parentheses, exclude the closing parenthesis
22:         // from our search range. Otherwise, we risk matching on calls, like `func(x)`, for which
23:         // the open and close parentheses are part of the `Arguments` node.
24:         //
25:         // There are a few other nodes that may have their own parentheses, but are fine to exclude:
26:         // - `Parameters`: The parameters to a function definition. Any expressions would represent
27:         //   default arguments, and so must be preceded by _at least_ the parameter name. As such,
28:         //   we won't mistake any parentheses for the opening and closing parentheses on the
29:         //   `Parameters` node itself.
30:         // - `Tuple`: The elements of a tuple. The only risk is a single-element tuple (e.g., `(x,)`),
31:         //    which must have a trailing comma anyway.
32:         let exclusive_parent_end = if parent.is_arguments() {
33:             parent.end() - ")".text_len()
34:         } else {
35:             parent.end()
36:         };
37:         SimpleTokenizer::new(source, TextRange::new(expr.end(), exclusive_parent_end))
38:     } else {
39:         SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(expr.end(), source)
40:     };
41: 
42:     let right_tokenizer = right_tokenizer
43:         .skip_trivia()
44:         .take_while(|token| token.kind == SimpleTokenKind::RParen);
45: 
46:     let left_tokenizer = BackwardsTokenizer::up_to(expr.start(), source, comment_ranges)
47:         .skip_trivia()
48:         .take_while(|token| token.kind == SimpleTokenKind::LParen);
49: 
50:     // Zip closing parenthesis with opening parenthesis. The order is intentional, as testing for
51:     // closing parentheses is cheaper, and `zip` will avoid progressing the `left_tokenizer` if
52:     // the `right_tokenizer` is exhausted.
53:     right_tokenizer
54:         .zip(left_tokenizer)
55:         .map(|(right, left)| TextRange::new(left.start(), right.end()))
56: }
57: 
58: /// Returns the [`TextRange`] of a given expression including parentheses, if the expression is
59: /// parenthesized; or `None`, if the expression is not parenthesized.
60: pub fn parenthesized_range(
61:     expr: ExpressionRef,
62:     parent: AnyNodeRef,
63:     comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
64:     source: &str,
65: ) -> Option<TextRange> {
66:     parentheses_iterator(expr, Some(parent), comment_ranges, source).last()
67: }

part.text:
Fixed. In `yield_in_for_loop.rs:111-116`, when the iterable is an unparenthesized tuple (`for e in x,:`), the generated fix now wraps it in parentheses, producing `yield from (x,)` instead of the invalid `yield from x,`.

Verified:
- Reproducer now fixes correctly: `yield from (x,)`
- All `ruff_linter` tests pass (2238 passed), including the UP028 snapshot tests that expect `yield from (1,)`
